summary: Defines a Type-Length-Value format for Cryptographically Generated Address extensions and updates RFC 3972. This provides a flexible way to add extra data into a CGA's parameters. It is a standards-track document.

plainLanguage.summary: A special kind of address is made from a secret key. This gives it a pocket in which extra labeled information can be tucked in a standard way.

questions: what is the cga extension field format
subtitle: A Type-Length-Value layout for the extension fields of Cryptographically Generated Addresses.

tldr.problem: CGA allows extension fields in its parameter data structure, but no standard format existed for packing more than one data item into them.
tldr.mechanism: Each item is encoded as a 16-bit Extension Type, a 16-bit Extension Data Length in octets, and variable-length Extension Data.
tldr.outcome: Future mechanisms can add data to CGA parameters in a uniform way, with a new IANA registry of extension types.

today: RFC 4581 is a Proposed Standard and updates RFC 3972. No later RFC obsoletes it.

sections.title: Why a Format Is Needed
sections.content: The CGA specification, RFC 3972, defines Extension Fields that let extra information ride in the CGA Parameter Data Structure. The authors expect more than one mechanism to use them, so this memo updates RFC 3972 and defines a Type-Length-Value format to make adding several data items simple.
sections.plainLanguage: Many things might want to use the pocket, so there needs to be a tidy way to pack them.

sections.title: The TLV Format
sections.content: Data items in Extension Fields MUST use this layout: a 16-bit Extension Type identifying the kind of field, a 16-bit unsigned Extension Data Length giving the length of the data in octets, and then the variable-length Extension Data, whose meaning depends on the type.
sections.plainLanguage: Each note starts with its kind, then how long it is, then the note itself.

sections.title: The Type Registry
sections.content: IANA maintains a registry called "CGA Extension Type" whose values are 16-bit unsigned integers. Future assignments are made through Standards Action. For experimental and testing use, the memo assigns 0xFFFD (Exp_FFFD), 0xFFFE (Exp_FFFE) and 0xFFFF (Exp_FFFF).
sections.plainLanguage: There is an official list of note kinds, with three kinds set aside for trying things out.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The format itself raises no security concerns. However, any new CGA extension needs proper security analysis to make sure it introduces no new vulnerabilities into the existing CGA schemes.
sections.plainLanguage: The label system is safe, but each new kind of note needs its own safety check.

fields.name: Extension Type
fields.desc: Identifier of the type of the Extension Field.

fields.name: Extension Data Length
fields.desc: Length of the Extension Data in octets.
